findings: Both raw notes independently preserve the same core problem but omit element-sign constraints, target range, API and no-solution behavior. The candidate correctly labels positivity, target > 0 and return-0 semantics as a reference contract rather than source truth.

The candidate does not trust the structured '(滑动窗口)' hint blindly: it explains that ordinary sum-window correctness depends on monotonicity and states exactly why strictly positive/nonnegative elements provide that property.

The Java implementation is complete and runnable, uses long for the window sum, updates while shrinking to obtain the shortest window, and states O(n) amortized time/O(1) auxiliary space with the pointer-movement proof.
The OpenJDK 21 fixture covers classic/exact/one-element optimum/no-solution/duplicate/empty/overflow-guard and invalid-input cases under the declared positive contract.

The negative-number boundary is not hand-waved: a prefix-sum plus monotonic-deque signed variant is distinguished from the primary sliding-window proof and was checked against a brute-force oracle on 5000 deterministic random cases.
All two source Question variants are covered; the 1-minute section has five main points, the 3-minute section adds mechanism and a runnable implementation, and follow-ups remain question-specific.
